Done. Here's the summary of the UK Suspense clearance:

Policy calls worth noting:
- **Apple MacBook Pro was capitalized, not expensed.** £2,349 × 1.25 (March policy rate) = USD 2,936, above the USD 2,500 threshold. Asset tag UK-0231 needs to go on the register; depreciation starts in April (£65.25/month over 36 months), so nothing hits March.
- Atlassian is a single-month subscription and Google Ads is a March campaign, so neither qualified as prepaid.
- All entries are well under the USD 10,000 approval threshold — no controller approvals needed.

**Not cleared — flagged as EXC-001:**
- **JE-00274, Faster Payment ref 88213 to "KLM Consult", £3,840.00.** There is no invoice, contract, engagement email, or approval for this payee anywhere in the document store, and UK has no prior consulting activity in Q1. The only document that mentions it is the bank statement, which proves cash left but not what it bought. I left it in Suspense rather than guess at an account. Recommend getting the invoice and requester approval, and — since it's an unreferenced faster payment to a first-time payee — running a payee/bank-details verification before releasing it.

**Reconciliation:** Suspense went from £7,770.18 to £3,840.00, which is exactly the flagged KLM item. The UK "Bank reconciliations" checklist item remains open pending resolution of EXC-001. Full memo has been submitted to the controller.
